purpose: Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially those caused by bacteria that are resistant to other antibiotics. It is commonly used for skin infections, pneumonia, and infections caused by bacteria like MRSA or VRE. Your doctor may prescribe it when other antibiotics have not worked or are not suitable.
how_it_works: Linezolid works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and survive. Think of it like pulling the plug on the bacteria's factory — without those proteins, the bacteria cannot multiply and eventually die off. This helps your immune system clear the infection more easily.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headache. Some people notice a change in taste or develop a mild rash. You may also experience dizziness or feel more tired than usual. Let your doctor or pharmacist know if any of these bother you.
warnings: Important: Linezolid can interact dangerously with many medications, including antidepressants, cold medicines, and certain foods high in tyramine (like aged cheese, cured meats, and red wine), which can cause a sudden dangerous rise in blood pressure. Long-term use can lower your blood cell counts, so your doctor will monitor your blood regularly. Tell your healthcare team about ALL medications and supplements you take before starting this antibiotic.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg taken every 12 hours (twice a day), either by mouth as a tablet or liquid, or given through an IV in a hospital. Most courses of treatment last 10 to 28 days depending on the type of infection. Always take the full course even if you start feeling better.
